text:
lia: FYI customer ACME opened a ticket — their app pods in the tenant VPC started getting NXDOMAIN for service.internal.acme after the AZ rebalancing last night. Public endpoints are fine, only internal resolution fails.

alex: Can you paste the minimal repro (dig/curl) from an affected host?

lia: From an app host inside acme-vpc (10.0.4.12):\n```
$ dig +short svc.api.internal.acme

;; -> no output, return code NXDOMAIN
$ dig svc.api.internal.acme @10.0.2.2 +short
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
$ curl -v http://svc.api.internal.acme/health
* Could not resolve host: svc.api.internal.acme\n```

sam: hmm, timed out to VPC resolver (10.0.2.2). Do they use Route53 Resolver inbound/endpoints or just VPC private hosted zones?

maria: Customer uses private hosted zones in their AWS account + cross-account associations for shared-service zone. There was an infra migration yesterday that associated a VRF/VPC replica into a shared account. Could be a hosted zone association conflict.

lia: I asked them to run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "internal.acme"` and `aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=acme-*` — they returned two private hosted zones with the same zone name in different accounts.

alex: That screams split-horizon / zone shadowing. If a VPC is accidentally associated with the wrong private hosted zone (same name), DNS answers from the wrong zone can be NXDOMAIN for records that live in the intended zone.

sam: Can you get the association list for the VPC? `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZONEID` and look at "VPCs".

lia: Got it. From ACME account: hosted-zone Z1 -> associated VPC: vpc-aaaa (correct). From shared infra account: hosted-zone Z2 -> associated VPC: vpc-aaaa (the same VPC!) 

maria: Oof — looks like the migration script in infra accidentally associated the shared-zone to the tenant VPC. That will shadow the tenant's records.

sre-bot: alert:resolver_rule_conflict detected for vpc-aaaa (tag:acme-prod) — potential private-hosted-zone name collision.

alex: Quick mitigation: disassociate the shared account hosted zone (Z2) from vpc-aaaa. Command: `aws route53 disassociate-vpc-from-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z2 --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-aaaa` (must be run from the account that owns Z2).

lia: I asked ACME to request infra team (shared account) to disassociate Z2. They performed the disassociation ~5m ago.

lia: Re-ran dig on app host: `dig +short svc.api.internal.acme @10.0.2.2` -> returns 10.251.8.12. `curl` now succeeds.

maria: Root cause: cross-account hosted zone association introduced during AZ/VPC migration shadowed the tenant's private hosted zone with same domain. DNS queries were answered by the wrong zone which didn't have the necessary records -> NXDOMAIN/timeouts.

sam: Follow-ups: (1) postmortem with infra team to stop automated cross-account associations for tenant VPCs, (2) add a resolver-rule association check in deployment pipeline to detect duplicate zone names, (3) add an SRE runbook for quick host-side debug (dig against .2 VPC resolver + `aws route53 get-hosted-zone` checks).

alex: Also recommend adding a monitoring alert for sudden increases in NXDOMAINs from VPC resolvers for specific tenant FQDNs.

lia: Customer confirmed full recovery and asked for a short RCA email. I'll draft and send. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: removed association Z2 <-> vpc-aaaa (initiated by infra-admin)

maria: Thanks all — keeping this thread for the RCA notes.

sam: tagging for postmortem: @maria @alex @lia :eyes:
